newsitem.title: USA: USDA reviewing Sun Diamond status after verdict.
newsitem.headline: USDA reviewing Sun Diamond status after verdict.

text.p: The U.S. Department of Agriculture said it was reviewing whether to allow Sun Diamond Growers of California to continue to participate in government programs after a verdict against the cooperative earlier Tuesday.
A jury found the cooperative guilty of giving illegal gifts and favors to former Agriculture Secretary Mike Espy in 1993 and 1994.

A spokeswoman for Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman said USDA was reviewing Sun Diamond's status as a supplier to the School Lunch program and a recipient of export promotion funds under the Market Access Program.
"USDA is considering the implications of the verdict and the Secretary expects to make a decision as soon as possible," spokeswoman Johna Pierce told Reuters.
Another USDA official said the department had been reviewing the situation since charges were laid against the cooperative several months ago.

The department was having difficulty deciding what steps to take, because any action would certainly harm farmers who were members of the cooperative and likely had no part in any wrongdoing, the official said.

For domestic feeding programs such as the School Lunch Program, USDA's Agricultural Marketing Service would first have to formally notify the cooperative of a proposal to bar it from the programs, and allow the cooperative to reply, the official said.
